notes.general_comments: The November 2023 Listening paper consisted of 37 multiple-choice questions. Candidates overall performed well in this paper and most attempted all questions. Candidates should take care when they transfer their answers onto the answer sheet and shade one letter only for Questions 1 to 34, and two letters for Questions 35 to 37. The French extracts heard by candidates gradually increased in terms of length and complexity and featured simple transactional exchanges, short monologues, conversations, and interviews. The emphasis of the questions moved from assessing the candidates’ ability to identify simple information contained in short factual pieces to testing their ability to understand specific information, descriptions of events, opinions, emotions, and explanations in longer extracts. The paper differentiated well.
notes.1-8: Overall, candidates performed very well in this exercise. The extracts were short, straightforward interactions. Most candidates answered Questions 1, 2 and 6 successfully. In Question 3, many candidates were familiar with appareil-photo; option D (porte-monnaie) was the most frequent incorrect answer. In Question 4, many candidates understood cravate; those who answered incorrectly chose options A and C in equal numbers. For Question 5, many candidates recognised fourchette; options A and B were the most frequent incorrect answers. In Question 7, some candidates did not understand hôtel de ville or perhaps did not notice the French flag on the picture; those who answered incorrectly mostly chose option D. For Question 8, many candidates recognised selfie; option B was the most common incorrect answer.
notes.9-14: In this exercise, candidates heard a longer extract about an advertisement for a village fair in Belgium. Overall, candidates performed very well in this exercise. All or nearly all the candidates answered Questions 9, 11 and 12 successfully. For Question 10, many candidates understood marionnettes. Most of those who answered incorrectly chose option B. For Question 13, some candidates did not recognise château; there was no pattern in the incorrect answers. For Question 14, many candidates were familiar with nuages; options D and A were the most frequent incorrect answers.
notes.15-19: This was a matching exercise in which candidates heard a conversation between two friends about clubs at the local leisure centre. Overall, candidates performed well in this exercise. Question 15 was attempted well. For Question 16, over three quarters of the cohort successfully matched pas libre with occupé ce jour-là and chose answer A. There was no clear pattern in the incorrect answers for the first two questions. A higher number of candidates answered Question 17 successfully and identified the reference to the past tense; those who answered incorrectly often chose statements A and C. Question 18 was also attempted well. There was no significant pattern in the incorrect answers. For Question 19, many candidates matched tournois avec d’autres clubs de la région with compétitions régionales and chose the correct answer D.
notes.20-28: In this exercise, candidates heard an interview with Yasmina who talked about her work as an au pair. The exercise represented a step up in the incline of difficulty of the test. For Question 20, many candidates correctly chose option C. Distractor A, the country where her penfriend lives, was the most frequent error. For Question 21, only a third of the candidates understood à la fac and successfully chose A; a quarter of the candidates incorrectly chose option B whilst the others selected distractor C. Question 22 was attempted well with over three quarters of the candidates correctly choosing option B; most of the others chose distractor A, which referred to the father. For Question 23, nearly three quarters of the candidates correctly matched disaient toujours ‘merci’ et ‘s’il te plait’ with polis and chose C; those who answered incorrectly mostly chose distractor A, which referred to Yasmine, not the children. In Question 24, candidates needed to listen carefully to the time phrases. Just over three quarters of the candidates successfully matched quelquefois je devais passer l’aspirateur with B; distractor C was the most frequent incorrect answer, a task that she performed every morning. Two thirds of the candidates answered Question 25 successfully. They needed to listen carefully to the tenses to identify what Yasmina did in her spare time in Scotland. Although il n’y avait pas d’équipe là-bas provided another clue, nearly a third of the candidates incorrectly chose distractor B. For Question 26, nearly two thirds of the cohort correctly selected B. Here candidates needed to focus on what she liked the most (ce que Yasmina a apprécié le plus); those who answered incorrectly nearly all chose distractor A. Question 27 was attempted well and many candidates successfully chose A. There was no pattern in the incorrect answers. For Question 28, over three quarters of the candidates successfully chose B. All the candidates who answered incorrectly chose distractor C, a career that Yasmina had considered but then dismissed in favour of something that would provide her with travel opportunities.
notes.29-34: In this exercise, candidates heard an interview with Timéo, who talked about his mobile restaurant, Le Régalbus. This was an appropriately demanding exercise at this stage of the paper. Question 29 was attempted well, and many candidates correctly chose B. Those who answered incorrectly often misunderstood the number and chose distractor A. For Question 30, almost two thirds of the candidates understood that the idea of a mobile restaurant came from Laurent, a friend of Timéo’s, and chose A. Nearly a quarter chose distractor D, which referred to the country Laurent visited, not Timéo; the others chose distractor B. For Question 31, nearly three quarters of the candidates successfully chose D. The most frequent error was C, although there was no reference to staff in that section; distractors A and B were selected in equal numbers. For Question 32, over half the cohort successfully matched des repas qui ne sont pas très chers with les prix sont raisonnables and chose C. Over a third of the candidates heard original and incorrectly chose distractor A. For Question 33, nearly three quarters of the candidates understood that c’est lui qui m’a donné envie de faire ce métier referred to a famous chef and chose A. Distractor B was the most frequent incorrect answer despite Timéo stating that his mother did not like cooking much. For Question 34, candidates needed to listen carefully to the various tenses. Over two thirds of the cohort successfully chose A; those who answered incorrectly either selected distractor D, something that Timéo used to do, or distractor C, something that he would like to do one day.
notes.35-37: In this exercise, candidates heard an interview with Alexandra, who talked about her latest travels on her bicycle. For each question, candidates had to identify two correct statements from a choice of five. This was an appropriately demanding and challenging exercise at this stage of the paper. For Question 35, just under half the candidates successfully selected D and over half correctly chose E. Nearly a third incorrectly chose distractor B: candidates needed to listen to the whole sentence as Alexandra explained that she ended up spending a whole year there. For Question 36, just over three quarters of the cohort successfully chose A and half correctly selected C. A quarter of the candidates heard animaux sauvages and incorrectly chose distractor E. They needed to listen carefully as Alexandra mentioned the presence of wild animals in the wild (a potential danger at night that she avoided by sleeping in villages), not on the roads. Statement B also proved a strong distractor. For Question 37, over half the cohort successfully selected B and half correctly chose D. Those who answered incorrectly often chose distractor E. Candidates needed to consider the verbs carefully as Alexandra explained that the night in the desert was the most memorable part of her journey, whereas statement E implied that it was something that she would have loved to do but did not.
